objective: Put the rig pipeline in the repo: a generated one-mesh animal model gets a full skeleton (knees, spine, neck, a tail of several bones), measured landmarks, clips keyed with planted feet and follow-through, and a board to pick them from (SHANNON, 2026-11-28: 'do anything necessary to make the animations and such good').
acceptance_criteria: run_creature.sh takes a creature folder with raw.glb to a rigged model and a board with no landmarks typed by hand (autoland.py)
Measured landmarks rig as well as hand-typed ones: on the Crystal Rhino, the Moon Lion and the Sun Cheetah the worst clip's stretch is within half a point of the hand rig's, and most clips are lower

One-shot clips are keyed with eases (a blow accelerates into its contact), a planted foot that moves steps in an arc, hips never pull a planted foot off the ground, and the tail follows through on a spring
A species has its own clip set (clipsets/rhino.py) and a variant its own power attack; lengths and blow times are the game's
verification: Blender 5.2, 2026-11-28. Stretched share of the surface, worst clip, measured landmarks against hand-typed ones on the same clip engine: Crystal Rhino 4.4 % (hand 4.7), Moon Lion 13.7 % against 13.3 (its fall; every other clip lower than by hand: gallop 3.6 against 5.0), Sun Cheetah 5.6 % against 8.9. A dead-straight measured leg gave the pole test no direction (front knees bending back, 10.6 %): each knee now gets a slight bend the way it folds. Found on the board: scale left on a springy bone by one clip built up over the next ones (the tail flung out by the nineteenth clip); bones are now reset and turned by pure rotations (scale off by 0.0 after all 21 clips). The Crystal Rhino's 21 clips rendered and looked through on contact sheets: feet planted, tail whole, the fall's horn clear of the ground.
notes: Tools only: nothing in the game reads them but export_game.py's output (STATION-199). The pipeline was worked out in a scratch folder over 2026-11-27 and 28 (the Sun Cheetah, the Moon Lion, the Crystal Rhino); this is its first commit. Not done here: turnaround concepts as 3D references, more bones (jaw, ears, wings, banners), an upright and a bird template, normal and roughness maps, batch runs. The Moon Lion's fall and slam still stretch over 10 %: its clip set (the shared one) needs its own keys.
